A report can place the observations beside their interpretation, an original document and a recording. Here the local media travels with the exported HTML; the external embed keeps its own availability.

## Make the evidence inspectable

::: columns {widths: 2-1}

::: column
```chart
type: bar
title: Mortality varied through the first three recorded months
data:
  inline:
    - { month: Apr, rate: 8.4 }
    - { month: May, rate: 10.8 }
    - { month: Jun, rate: 7.2 }
encoding: { x: month, y: rate }
axes: { y: { label: 'Annualized deaths per 1,000' } }
```

*Source: Nightingale's mortality record, April–June 1854; each displayed annualized rate sums the causes for that month.*
:::

::: column
```metric
value: 8.4
label: Annualized deaths per 1,000, April 1854
```

```callout
kind: hold
title: Keep the unit with the number
body: An annualized rate cannot be read as the number of people who died that month. Inspect the full observations before comparing periods.
```
:::

:::

```table
title: The rates behind the chart, 1854
data:
  inline:
    - { month: Apr, rate: 8.4 }
    - { month: May, rate: 10.8 }
    - { month: Jun, rate: 7.2 }
columns:
  - { key: month, label: Month }
  - { key: rate, label: 'Annualized deaths per 1,000', format: number, align: right }
```

*Source: Florence Nightingale's Crimean War mortality record, via [HistData](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/Rdatasets/doc/HistData/Nightingale.html). The displayed rates sum preventable disease, wounds and other causes in each of the first three months. They are annualized rates, not monthly death counts. The April metric is authored from the same observations.*

## A recording gives a primary source a voice

```audio
src: media/apollo-step.mp3
title: Neil Armstrong's first words on the Moon
caption: Apollo 11, 21 July 1969 UTC. NASA Historical Sounds; public-domain mission recording.
transcript: media/transcript.md
```

```video
src: media/apollo-step.mp4
title: Buzz Aldrin comes down the lunar module ladder
caption: A 12-second silent excerpt from the Apollo 11 television video that NASA partially restored in 2009. NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center; public domain.
poster: media/apollo-poster.jpg
transcript: media/video-transcript.md
captions: media/captions.vtt
```

The [NASA audio collection](https://www.nasa.gov/historical-sounds/) supplies the recording; the [NASA Image and Video Library](https://images.nasa.gov/details/Apollo_11_moonwalk_montage_720p) supplies the film, a two-minute montage of the moonwalk video that [NASA partially restored in 2009](https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/10451); [NASA's media guidelines](https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/) say its footage is not subject to copyright in the United States. The silent film excerpt starts 41 seconds into `Apollo_11_moonwalk_montage_720p~orig.mov`; its original soundtrack is omitted. Captions describe the silent scene; the audio player has its own transcript.

## Guide attention across the original diagram

```scrolly
title: Read Nightingale's comparison
image:
  src: media/nightingale.jpg
  alt: Nightingale's original two-period mortality diagram.
steps:
  - title: Two periods, one unit
    text: Begin with both circles. Each compares causes of mortality through an April-to-March year.
    view: { x: 0, y: 0, zoom: 1 }
  - title: The first winter
    text: Focus on the larger right-hand diagram. Its blue area records deaths from preventable disease; the printed legend explains that the wedges encode area.
    view: { x: 0.35, y: 0.05, zoom: 1.6 }
    highlight: { x: 0.55, y: 0.1, w: 0.4, h: 0.7 }
```

## A formula needs its assumptions

For an independent Bernoulli sample, the estimated standard error of a sample proportion is

$$
\operatorname{SE}(\hat p) = \sqrt{\frac{\hat p(1-\hat p)}{n}}
$$

Here $n$ is the sample size and $\hat p$ the observed proportion. It is an estimate under a sampling model, not a formula for Nightingale's annualized rates.
